svg.title: How a request flows through the Lock Family
svg.desc: An agent (Claude Code, Codex, lea) runs in its harness with a Lock client, an MCP server that holds no credential. The client reaches the lock over a socket; the lock holds the credentials and the only connection to the database, RabbitMQ, files, HTTP or logs. The lock sends a masked ticket to the hub; the hub passes it to lox run, which the human keeps open in a terminal of their own, outside the harness. lox run decides, by an auto rule or by asking the human; the hub signs the decision and the lock runs the request only on it, then masks the result for the agent. The agent never talks to the hub, and the hub never sees a query or a result in clear. Four scenarios loop: 1, a SELECT on profile replica is approved by an auto rule, no question, and masked rows come back; 2, the first request on profile primary makes the lock send a connect ticket, lox run asks y/n once for the session, and the lock connects on the signed decision; 3, an UPDATE is always asked, approved with y and run; 4, a DELETE is asked and denied with n, the lock never runs it and the agent is told it was denied.
